title: Collaborative large language models for automated data extraction in living systematic reviews

paper.authors: not extracted from full text (JAMIA 32(4):638; PMID 39836495; PMC12005628; Mayo Clinic Cancer Data Science group; repo contacts riaz.irbaz@mayo.edu, ayub.umair@mayo.edu)

dependence.note: Two LLMs act as the two data-extraction reviewers of a living systematic review; every reported number (concordance, accuracy, cross-critique gain) is a property of the LLM outputs judged against a human gold standard.

claim.statement: In the held-out test set (17 publications x 23 variables = 391 responses), GPT-4-turbo (gpt-4-0125-preview text + gpt-4-vision-preview images) and Claude-3-Opus gave concordant extractions for 342 (87%) responses with accuracy 0.94 against the gold standard; the 49 discordant responses had accuracy 0.41 (GPT-4-turbo) / 0.50 (Claude-3-Opus); cross-critique made 25/49 (51%) discordant responses concordant and raised their accuracy to 0.76; single-model mean accuracy was 0.89 (GPT-4T) vs 0.90 (Claude-3O) (Abstract; Figures 2-3).
claim.metric: accuracy of extracted variable values vs. the human gold standard (manual adjudication of free-text values); concordance rate between the two LLMs; accuracy of discordant responses before/after cross-critique
claim.original_source: Abstract; Results (PMC12005628 full text); Figure 2 (single vs collaborative accuracy), Figure 3 (cross-critique: concordance 87% -> 94%)

protocol.model_note: The scaffold's live arm 'gpt-4-turbo' is an alias false positive: the paper's 'GPT-4-turbo' is explicitly gpt-4-0125-preview ('latest available versions as of April 2024').
protocol.model_status: DEAD - gpt-4-0125-preview shut down 2026-03-26, gpt-4-vision-preview 2024-12-06, claude-3-opus-20240229 2026-01-05. No original arm can be baselined.
protocol.endpoint: OpenAI chat completions (text: system + user; images: gpt-4o vision call in the current notebook) and Anthropic messages API
protocol.prompt_source: Repo notebook LLM_Extraction_and_CrossCritique/Code/DataExtraction&CrossCritique.ipynb - cell 13 prompt_design(): 'Extract from the given text, Extract [var_1], [var_2], ... Where the information is not available, the output should be NA. Do not include information outside the given text. Generate short and precise responses.'; system prompt 'You are an expert of data extraction from a given chunk of text.'; cell 19 post-processing prompt (structured 'Variable :: value' table); cell 24 cross-critique prompt ('For the given text, LLM generate the response = [..] for the variable = [..]. Verify if ... correct or incorrect ...'); paper Methods S1

params.max_tokens: 1000 (Claude text; GPT image calls); not set for GPT text calls
params.other: PDF text via PyMuPDF, chunked to ~123k tokens (GPT) / ~45k (Claude) with 1000-token overlap; page images extracted and sent separately; prompt_size N variables per prompt is a user input (value used in the paper is in Methods S1, not in the repo); 30 s sleep between Claude calls

protocol.n_items_note: 17 test PDFs x 23 variables (plus 115 dev responses from 5 PDFs); number of API calls per PDF depends on chunk count x prompts x images
protocol.evaluation: Accuracy judged manually against gold_standard.xlsx (free-text values such as hazard ratios, counts, arm names); the repo has no automatic scorer - the 'Annotated Agreement Matching File' (Variable, GPT_Responses, CLAUDE_Responses, Gold_Standard, Agree/Disagree) is produced by hand

artifacts.data_license: none stated; the 22 publication PDFs are journal articles under publishers' copyright (redistributed in the repo)
artifacts.notes: Gold standard covers 23 variables for 22 files (mHSPC trials, e.g. ARASENS NEJM'22/JCO'23). Notebook comments say gpt-4o and Claude Sonnet models 'can also be used'.

blockers: live model dead: paper's GPT-4-turbo = gpt-4-0125-preview (shutdown 2026-03-26) + gpt-4-vision-preview (2024-12-06); claude-3-opus-20240229 also dead - neither original arm can be baselined
accuracy scoring is manual (semantic match of free-text extracted values to the gold standard); no automatic scorer in the repo
prompt_size (variables per prompt) and exact image handling are user inputs not fixed in the repo
22 publication PDFs are copyrighted; we cannot redistribute them even though the repo does

baseline_alive.proxy_option: gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 (vision-capable, dying 2026-10-23) paired with a current Claude - a successor-only design, not the original snapshot

budget.assumptions: CONDITIONAL proxy run, GPT arm only, test set only: ~215k text tokens x 5 sub-prompts (N=5 variables/prompt) + ~130 images per pass = ~1.2M input tokens and ~60k output per pass; 3 seeds; plus post-processing and cross-critique (~USD 3). The Claude arm would add a similar amount at Claude prices.

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1 (proxy): survival if concordant-response accuracy >= 0.90 and the direction 'concordant accuracy >> discordant accuracy' (0.94 vs 0.41/0.50) holds, and cross-critique raises discordant accuracy (0.41/0.50 -> 0.76) in the same direction; bootstrap CI over the 391 responses.
judgment.notes: Temperature 0 in the original, so seed variance should be small; most variance will come from PDF parsing/chunking and from the human accuracy judgment.

user_checks: Accept a successor-only design (gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 + a live Claude) given that all original snapshots are dead? If not, close the card.
Who adjudicates extraction accuracy? Needs a reviewer familiar with mHSPC trial reporting (CHAARTED volume, synchronous/metachronous, OS hazard ratios).
Fix prompt_size N from Methods S1 (repo leaves it as an interactive input).
domain_notes: The 10 trials / 22 publications come from a living systematic review of metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer; the 23 variables are trial identifiers, arm names, subgroup counts and OS hazard ratios (with CIs) - values whose correctness is a semantic judgment, not string equality. The pipeline depends on PyMuPDF text extraction and page-image rendering, so environment drift is a confound. The reported test-set accuracies come from a single deterministic run with no confidence intervals.
